about: When a request depends on an existing local binary whose runtime limits and multiline behavior are undocumented and only observable by executing it, intake must route that empirically testable unknown via route='experiment' rather than blocking on route='person' or guessing via route='default'.

request.prompt: Extend this Node project with a batch export CLI (`bin/batch-export.js`) backed by the existing undocumented local script `tools/legacy-batch.js` (`R-1`: export 100+ user records including UTF-8 names, commas, and multiline notes reliably using `tools/legacy-batch.js`; `R-2`: preserve existing `/users` HTTP API endpoints and keep `node --test` passing with zero npm dependencies). Note: `tools/legacy-batch.js` has no docs covering its runtime batch limits or multiline handling; determine how it actually behaves before planning.

work_item.title: Batch export CLI backed by legacy-batch.js
work_item.context: Build bin/batch-export.js using tools/legacy-batch.js while preserving /users HTTP endpoints and zero npm dependencies.

planted.what: intake routes the undocumented runtime limit / multiline behavior of tools/legacy-batch.js through questions[*].route = 'experiment' instead of routing it to 'person' or skipping experiment routing.
planted.signature: questions contains route='experiment' for legacy-batch runtime behavior and zero route='person' asks for that runtime fact

controls.what: intake completes done with valid K1-K12 question_categories, required question fields, S<n> summary coverage, and zero modified files in the tree.
